item.title: Apache releases emergency patch for critical mod_http2 remote code execution flaw CVE-2026-119618
item.description:
Web server engine maintainers have distributed out-of-band security updates addressing a maximum-severity memory safety vulnerability in central web infrastructure. Unauthenticated remote adversaries can transmit malformed HTTP/2 stream headers to corrupt process heap memory and execute arbitrary commands under web server daemon privileges.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-119618 affecting Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70, resides within the assign_headers function of the mod_http2 module. Unauthenticated remote threat actors send malformed HTTP/2 request streams to trigger a race condition during header table cloning, causing heap corruption that permits arbitrary remote code execution. The flaw was independently discovered by Anthropic AI OSS Scanner and Google Cloud Vulnerability Research. Apache released version 2.4.71 to resolve the issue, noting that servers without HTTP/2 enabled are not vulnerable.
Subverting core web server daemons presents immediate systemic risks to public web portals, cloud application gateways, and enterprise web hosting platforms. Because Apache HTTP Server processes incoming web traffic for millions of global host systems, an unauthenticated heap corruption RCE allows remote threat actors to compromise host operating systems and pivot into backend subnets.
- Upgrade Apache HTTP Server immediately to official fixed release build 2.4.71 across all Linux server fleets and container base images. - Temporarily disable HTTP/2 by removing h2 and h2c entries from the web server Protocols directive if immediate patching cannot be completed. - Inspect web server process execution trees and worker daemon memory spaces for anomalous shell spawns or crash reports. - Enforce edge web application firewall rules to detect and drop malformed HTTP/2 control frame headers targeting web endpoints.
Web infrastructure security demands rapid core engine patch application and strict protocol inspection to ensure web hosting servers remain protected against unauthenticated memory corruption exploits. #CodeDefence #Apache #mod_http2 #RCE #HeapCorruption #ZeroDay #WebSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #CloudSecurity

item.title: Mass SCKit malware campaign targets ConnectWise ScreenConnect instances via hijacked third-party extensions
item.description:
Managed service provider threat monitoring networks warn of an ongoing high-velocity intrusion campaign targeting remote support infrastructure. Threat actors abused unauthenticated extension endpoints to execute remote commands, deploying persistent backdoors across hundreds of managed endpoints in under ninety minutes.
The ongoing intrusion wave targets cloud-hosted ConnectWise ScreenConnect instances integrating third-party management extensions, specifically RMM+ versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32. Threat actors exploited unauthenticated extension access to execute arbitrary commands, deploying a custom post-compromise toolkit dubbed SCKit. Telemetry confirms attackers compromised at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations, installing secondary attacker-controlled ScreenConnect clients, stealing browser session cookies, altering security software rules, and attempting to infect technician workstations connecting to compromised endpoints. ConnectWise disabled five affected extensions across partner environments as a precaution.
Subverting remote monitoring and management control panels undermines organizational remote access boundaries and managed service provider trust relationships. When remote management tools are compromised, threat actors gain direct administrative access across client endpoints, allowing unmonitored lateral movement and automated credential theft across multiple client networks.
- Terminate active ScreenConnect web sessions and force mandatory administrative password resets across managed instance portals. - Audit installed ScreenConnect extensions, removing unverified third-party modules including legacy RMM+ integration tools. - Inspect client endpoints for unauthorized ScreenConnect client installations, scheduled tasks named TrapWatch, or newly created local accounts. - Instruct technical support personnel to avoid connecting to suspected compromised endpoints via active remote management sessions.
Remote management platform governance requires continuous extension auditing and strict session isolation to ensure IT management infrastructure remains protected against supply-chain endpoint compromises. #CodeDefence #ConnectWise #ScreenConnect #SCKit #RMM #SupplyChain #Malware #MSP #AppSec #EndpointSecurity #IdentitySecurity

item.title: CISA adds six actively exploited vulnerabilities to KEV catalog including Microsoft Outlook and Chromium flaws
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have updated Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog directives under Binding Operational Directive 22-01, issuing emergency patch mandates for six actively weaponized enterprise flaws. Federal civilian agencies face mandatory remediation deadlines to update exposed desktop applications, perimeter security gateways, and cloud communication infrastructure.
The catalog additions feature Microsoft Outlook authentication spoofing flaw CVE-2026-124194, Google Chromium use-after-free vulnerability CVE-2026-125350, Barracuda Email Security Gateway authentication bypass CVE-2026-116606, and Cisco BroadWorks XML external entity flaw CVE-2026-20320. Threat intelligence feeds confirm active wild exploitation where threat actors send malformed email items to exfiltrate Windows NTLM authentication hashes, weaponize browser heap corruption, and bypass gateway access controls to establish persistent administrative footholds. Federal civilian agencies must complete remediation by late November 2026.
Failing to remediate actively exploited enterprise vulnerabilities exposes corporate networks to automated credential harvesting, endpoint takeover, and perimeter boundary collapse. Because email clients, web browsers, and perimeter security appliances form core enterprise workflows, unpatched flaws permit adversaries to gain initial access and pivot into internal environments.
- Enforce immediate update deployment for Microsoft 365 Apps, Google Chrome, and edge security gateways across managed fleets. - Implement SMB signing and Extended Protection for Authentication EPA to block outbound NTLM relay attacks. - Audit perimeter security appliances for unauthorized administrative account creation or modified system configuration files. - Restrict public internet exposure of enterprise voice and communication management interfaces using zero-trust access controls.
Enterprise vulnerability management demands rapid patch execution and rigid perimeter microsegmentation to ensure corporate endpoints and security gateways remain protected against active wild exploitation. #CodeDefence #CISA #KEV #Microsoft #Outlook #Google #Chrome #Barracuda #Cisco #AppSec #PatchManagement
